transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-05-21 11:00 AM PT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Miller (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Luis Ortega (Redwood CSM) — Marta Ruiz (Atlas Procurement), Evan Chen (Atlas Security), Samir Patel (Atlas FP&A), Claire Du (Atlas Legal)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
- Purpose: align on onboarding path for Atlas Retail (pilot -> pilot acceptance -> procurement gating), cover MSA/DPA redlines, SLA expectations, pricing approval steps, and technical benchmark plan.
- Main blockers: DPA exceptions (data residency clauses), KMS/privileged key handling, egress cost sensitivity, exec-level pricing signoff timeline.
- Outcome: Redwood to provide redline suggestions, run benchmarks, Atlas to consolidate exceptions and deliver commit targets.

Topics:
- MSA/DPA redlines and exceptions
- SLA uptime and rollback/penalty language
- KMS / encryption keying model (BYOK vs Redwood-managed)
- Pilot scope, acceptance criteria and benchmarking window
- Pricing tiers, egress and committed volume discounts

Action items (brief): see metadata list above.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Jordan Miller from Redwood — AE. Really glad we could do this alignment call. intention today is to map the legal flightpath and the pricing runway so procurement and finance have a clear view.
[00:12] Marta: Hi Jordan, Marta here — head of procurement at Atlas. Thanks, yeah we want something that fits our quarter end review, so timing is tight.
[00:18] Evan: Evan, security. We'll be focused on the DPA and KMS handling.
[00:22] Samir: Samir from FP&A — we'll own the commit numbers and run the pricing approval.
[00:25] Claire: Claire, legal counsel — I'll consolidate any contract exceptions.
[00:28] Priya: Thanks all, Priya Shah, SE at Redwood. I'll own the technical benchmarking part and pilot orchestration.
[00:32] Jordan: Cool. Quick agenda check — we planned 40-ish minutes: 1) procurement/legal asks, 2) technical risk items, 3) pricing path and timeline, 4) next steps. Any additions?
[00:41] Marta: No, that's good. We just want to make sure DPA exceptions are surfaced and SLA penalties are clear. Also egress fees — our egress budget is pretty constrained.
[00:48] Jordan: Understood. On the DPA piece, we've already noted Atlas wants a data residency clause for EU-only residency for the customer records used in model prompts. Claire, is that the primary ask?
[00:58] Claire: Yes, and also a requirement for customer-controlled key management for sensitive PII flows. We prefer BYOK but can evaluate Redwood's HSM if we get the attestation.
[01:07] Evan: Just to add, we'll need SOC 2 type II and a pen-test summary. Also looking for audit log retention for 13 months.
[01:16] Priya: Quick note — Redwood Private supports a VPC deployment and optional customer-managed KMS; for hosted we do offer KMS integration with external key stores, but there's an initial sync necessary.
[01:28] Marta: That's right — the procurement team will escalate if hosted requires pass-through keys. It affects our legal assessment.
[01:33] Jordan: Ok so action item: Claire to send consolidated DPA exceptions; Redwood legal to propose redline language. We'll aim for a suggested MSA/DPA redline by next Monday, 2025-05-26. Does that timeline work?
[01:44] Claire: That's achievable from our side to review once we see Redwood's suggested language.
[01:48] Samir: On pricing, quick question — do you have a committed discount ladder tied to token volumes or to qps/throughput? We need to map to our forecast.
[01:58] Jordan: Good question. Our standard is a volume-based tiered discount (tokens/month), and a dedicated capacity option for guaranteed throughput with flat monthly commit. We can map both to your forecast.
[02:08] Samir: For initial budgeting we need an estimate assuming a 6-month pilot with a 3-node dedicated pool if the pilot needs stable latency. Is that something you'd price out?
[02:16] Priya: Yes, we can run a pricing mock. But also, one thought — if latency is less strict we can do hosted with cache and batching to reduce cost. There's a tradeoff: dedicated = predictable tail latency and throughput; hosted = lower ops but potential jitter.
[02:32] Evan: Can you quantify jitter? For our user-facing flows, 95th percentile matters.
[02:36] Priya: We'll run a 48-hour benchmark on your sample traffic to produce p50/p95/p99 numbers and token cost projections. We'll include both hosted and dedicated profiles.
[02:45] Jordan: That's a concrete next step. Priya will request sample traffic; Priya, can you put that in an action item?
[02:51] Priya: Yep. I'll follow up right after this call.
[02:54] Jordan: On SLAs — we typically offer 99.9% for hosted customers, and for Dedicated we can do higher SLOs and custom penalties in the MSA. We have fallback policies and auto-failover across regions to help with uptime.
[03:08] Marta: Procurement will likely push for a 99.95% for our production tier. Penalties are a big negotiation point. What's your typical liquidated damages formula?
[03:18] Jordan: We usually structure credits based on downtime minutes beyond SLO, with caps. We can propose a tiered credit schedule; if you need a stricter liquidated damages form we can elevate to legal, but that's uncommon for smaller pilots.
[03:29] Claire: We prefer explicit credits and a lower cap for the pilot. We'll draft language and propose numbers.
[03:35] Samir: Also curious about rollback/rollback windows — if we push a model and quality drops, how do rollbacks and rollouts work, and is there an SLA for quality regressions?
[03:44] Priya: Redwood supports model version pinning and automated rollback policies. We don't generally have an SLA for output quality, because it's a model property, but we do have runbooks and can do A/B rollouts and can configure automatic fallback to prior model variants.
[04:00] Evan: Security question — audit logs, redaction controls, and session-level access? How granular are your RBAC controls?
[04:07] Priya: RBAC is role-based with token-level scoping; you can restrict routes and models per team. Audit logs capture request metadata, timestamps, and anonymized responses if you want. Note: redaction is optional but we cannot guarantee perfect PII removal — that's why BYOK and customer-side preprocessing are suggested for sensitive flows.
[04:26] Marta: Egress — we saw earlier notes about egress fees. For high volume use cases, that can blow our budget. What levers exist?
[04:33] Jordan: Egress is typically charged on dedicated/private when data leaves your VPC or across regions. For hosted, we fold some egress into the token unit cost but large bulk transfers can be priced separately. We can propose an egress cap for the pilot or include egress in the committed volume pricing.
[04:48] Samir: Good. We'll need a modeled example: projected monthly token usage plus egress line items to present to finance.
[04:55] Jordan: We'll include that in the pricing memo.
[04:57] [05:00] Priya: Technical note: For the benchmark, please send sample payloads that reflect average sequence lengths — long context vs short prompts matter a lot for throughput and cost.
[05:08] Marta: We'll prepare two sample sets: customer support dialogue (short prompts) and knowledge-base retrieval + long context (long prompts).
[05:15] Priya: Perfect. Also include concurrency profile — do you expect large bursts or steady qps?
[05:19] Marta: Bursty, typical retail flash events — we'll note that.
[05:23] Jordan: Ok, so timeline — pilot start ideally by Jun 2 to align with your quarter. That gives us time for redlines and benchmarks. Is that acceptable?
[05:32] Samir: That would be tight but workable if legal turnaround is quick.
[05:36] Claire: We'll try to get the exceptions list within the week.
[05:39] Jordan: Great. Any other procurement items?
[05:42] Marta: Payment terms — standard 60 days is our org's default. Will that be a blocker for you?
[05:47] Jordan: Redwood standard for enterprise is net 45; net 60 is acceptable at scale but may affect initial pilot billing. We can agree to net 60 for the long-term contract; pilot could be billed on shorter terms. We can note that in the MSA redline.
[05:58] Samir: For pricing approvals we need an internal memo. Can Redwood include a brief one-page pricing rationale and an attachable TCO example?
[06:07] Jordan: Yes — we'll prepare a TCO spreadsheet and one-pager explaining commitment tiers and expected unit economics.
[06:11] Marta: Perfect.
[06:13] [06:15] Priya: Quick bit of transparency — some of the open-source model names in our catalog may be mis-transcribed in older docs — e.g. you might see "Redwood optimiser" or references to quantized runtimes; don't rely on older model names. We'll be explicit in the benchmark report which model and quantization is used.
[06:31] Evan: For compliance, do you provide export control or restricted data handling options? We may have EU-only PII for customers.
[06:38] Jordan: Yes, we support region-specific deployments and data plane residency in EU regions; for stricter controls we recommend Private deployment inside your VPC or an on-prem package.
[06:48] Claire: If we go private, what does the onboarding time look like?
[06:51] Priya: Private deploys are longer — typically 6-8 weeks for the full stack and KMS integration, depends on your infra team bandwidth. Hosted pilot is ~2 weeks to provision and run initial tests.
[07:03] Marta: Given our timeline, we probably start hosted pilot and decide mid-pilot if we need private.
[07:09] Jordan: That is a reasonable approach.
[07:12] [07:15] Samir: One more ask — can we get sample SLA language for dedicated capacity that includes a 99.95% SLO and a credits schedule? We'll need that to present to our ops committee.
[07:25] Jordan: Yes, Redwood legal can draft a dedicated-SLA addendum with a credit table. We'll include it in the redline packet.
[07:31] Claire: For DPA exceptions, one specific clause — cross-border transfer limitation for European customer data. We'll flag that.
[07:38] Priya: Noted. For bench privileges — we'll need credentials to a staging VPC or access tokens with a bounded scope. We'll coordinate offline on secure sharing.
[07:48] Marta: Security can coordinate with Priya after this meeting. Evan will be the technical point.
[07:52] Evan: happy to.
[07:54] [08:00] Jordan: Wrap-up summary: 1) Claire to send DPA exceptions this week; 2) Redwood to deliver MSA/DPA redline + dedicated SLA draft by 2025-05-26; 3) Priya to request sample datasets and kick off 48-hr benchmark aiming to deliver p50/p95/p99 plus cost projection by 2025-05-28; 4) Jordan to deliver pricing memo and TCO one-pager by 2025-05-23; 5) Samir to provide commit target by 2025-05-29.
[08:31] Marta: Good recap. We'll try to get Claire's list before Friday.
[08:36] Jordan: Anything else?
[08:38] Samir: No, thanks.
[08:40] Claire: No, thanks everyone.
[08:42] Jordan: Great, we'll follow up in email with links to the folder and the timeline. Thanks all.

Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings corrected inline; some acronyms may appear as "sock two" (SOC 2) or "SAM-el" (SAML) in raw transcript. There was light crosstalk during the procurement questions.
